events.title: Apple announces the iPhone
events.description: A touchscreen device combines phone, music and internet functions.

events.title: The financial crisis intensifies
events.description: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy. Authorities support other financial firms as stress spreads.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon disaster
events.description: An offshore drilling explosion kills workers and leads to a major oil spill.

what_happened_next.text:
Disney gained about 47% over five years, while Toyota fell around 15% and Exxon Mobil gained about 8%. Bonds gained more than either broad share basket. These different results came through the financial crisis, which made the path difficult even for investments that finished higher.

The company stories were different too. Toyota reported a ¥437 billion loss for the year ending in March 2009 as car sales fell and the strong yen added pressure. Disney agreed to buy Marvel in 2009, adding thousands of characters to its movie and product business. ExxonMobil’s 2009 earnings fell sharply from 2008 as energy prices weakened.

The Deepwater Horizon disaster followed in 2010, bringing a deadly oil spill and a major cleanup. It affected the whole energy industry’s setting, but it should not be treated as a simple explanation for Exxon’s five-year return. Disney’s gain also does not mean every entertainment company would do well. Bonds provided another kind of investment, with a different path from company shares. The final balances show how much company results can differ, even when all three start as large, familiar businesses.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Katrina recovery, energy supplies and competition in cars and entertainment were prominent concerns.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The mix of assets mattered through a severe financial shock. A famous company could finish below its starting value while a government-bond estimate gained.
reflection.what_faded_away: A record earnings announcement described a past quarter, not the next five years. A confident new leader also had no control over every event ahead.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The crisis and the exact investment ranking were unknown. Today’s chart makes a difficult period look much simpler than it was.

hot:2005-09:toyota.text: In May 2009, Toyota reported a net loss of ¥437 billion for the year ending in March. It sold 1.34 million fewer vehicles than a year earlier as demand fell during the financial crisis. A stronger yen also reduced the value of money earned overseas, adding to the pressure on profits.

hot:2005-09:disney.text: In August 2009, Disney agreed to buy Marvel, adding more than 5,000 comic-book characters to its entertainment business. Disney planned to bring these stories to more people through movies and other products around the world. The deal gave it a much larger collection of characters to build businesses around.

hot:2005-09:exxonmobil.text: ExxonMobil reported in February 2010 that its 2009 profit fell to $19.3 billion from $45.2 billion in 2008. Lower oil and gas prices and weaker profits from refining hurt its results during the global downturn. The company still made money, but its annual profit was less than half the previous year’s.
